newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Norilsk says labour deal holding up well.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Norilsk says labour deal holding up well.

text.p: Russia's financially troubled Norilsk Nickel NKEL.RTS metals group said on Thursday that a peace deal obliging workers not to disrupt output before July was holding up well despite a backlog in salaries.

A company statement said managers from the group's flagship plant -- one of the world's major mining and smelting complexes -- met trade union leaders and both sides were satisfied with progress in talks on wage and other arrears.

Norilsk, a top global supplier of nickel, platinum group metals, cobalt and copper, averted calls for strikes in March and April after management reached a temporary agreement with workers running to July 1.
Norilsk said wage arrears had been halved to one and a half months and would be paid off according to a timetable agreed with workers. Summer vacation subsidies had also been paid.

RAO Norilsky Nikel, which accounts for around 85 percent of Russian nickel output, plans to become the world's largest nickel producer this year by expanding production by 20 percent to 213,000 tonnes.
But gas supplies to the main production complex have been cut by nearly one third over unpaid energy debts since early June and officials have said output may be affected.
